$comment: Compressed npm download size must be strictly below 10 MB decimal (10,000,000 bytes). The historical baseline is informational for packed size. The editor data (@aceshooting/lyra-ide) and the locale catalogs (@aceshooting/lyra-translations) ship in companion packages, so the unpacked ceiling now enforces the 25% reduction from that baseline without an exception; file-count derivation reserves seven artifacts beyond the measured 308-alias inventory. Each companion has its own hard ceilings under `companions`. Required public artifacts and artifact hygiene are validated independently of every size ceiling. The UI unpacked ceiling covers the exact 20,989,217-byte estimate with 31 bytes of allowance; the actual archive measures 20,988,616 bytes after manifest normalization. The translations unpacked and IDE packed ceilings cover exact measurements of 5,823,466 and 1,657,629 bytes with 22 and 35 bytes of allowance. All other package ceilings and the historical reduction baseline remain unchanged. The final 29.1.0 changelog section raises the UI estimate to 20,989,500 bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary, as does the translations unpacked ceiling over its 5,823,499-byte measurement. 29.2.0: the UI unpacked estimate of 20,998,169 bytes (regional catalogs, translation tooling docs, coverage-neutral source) advances its ceiling to 20,998,208; four regional catalogs add 41 translation files, so the translations file ceiling is 911 and its unpacked ceiling advances to 5,838,912 over a 5,838,869-byte measurement. The 29.2.0 changelog sections raise the UI unpacked estimate to 21,000,814, the translations unpacked size to 5,839,097 and the IDE packed size to 1,657,673 bytes; each ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. 29.2.x: the pnpm skills-approval note raises the UI unpacked estimate to 21,000,964 bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. The 29.2.1 changelog sections raise the UI unpacked estimate to 21,001,432 bytes and the translations unpacked size to 5,839,226 bytes; each ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. The 29.2.2 chart color correction and release notes measure 21,002,693 unpacked UI bytes; the translations release notes measure 5,839,322 unpacked bytes. Only these two ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundary. 30.0.0: the immutable identity collections, lr-map camera commands, the immutable-collections migration rule and the v29 to v30 migration guide measure 21,044,702 unpacked UI bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. The same 30.0.0 change grows the editor data (@aceshooting/lyra-ide) to 1,660,919 packed bytes; its packed ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. Map overlays, their public declarations and documentation measure 21,080,185 unpacked UI bytes; generated editor data measures 1,663,119 packed and 10,355,047 unpacked bytes. Only these three failing ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundary. The 3D foundation translation additions use the approved unpacked ceiling of 5,897,984 bytes. The optional 3D views (WebGL graph and embedding renderers, image and video panoramas), the owned map resources and drawing, their declarations, documentation and localized strings measure 21,525,287 unpacked UI bytes and 6,070,414 unpacked translation bytes; both ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundary. Their editor data (@aceshooting/lyra-ide) measures 1,685,101 packed and 10,459,385 unpacked bytes; both ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundary. The map companion (@aceshooting/lyra-map) measures 4,006,720 unpacked bytes, exactly a 64-byte boundary, which becomes its ceiling. The CI-generated editor data then measures 1,688,127 packed and 10,477,886 unpacked bytes; both ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundary. The companion-package job packs the same UI tarball from the shared build artifact at 21,525,899 unpacked bytes, so the UI ceiling covers that larger measurement at the next 64-byte boundary (21,525,952). Loading lr-map's optional features on demand adds module-boundary code: the regenerated UI tarball measures 21,537,343 unpacked bytes, and the ceiling keeps the 612-byte allowance for the shared-artifact pack at the next 64-byte boundary (21,537,984). The new lr-chart-3d brings the regenerated UI tarball to 21,601,626 unpacked bytes; the ceiling keeps the 612-byte shared-artifact allowance at the next 64-byte boundary (21,602,240). The lr-chart-3d strings bring the translations package to 6,112,511 unpacked bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary. Regenerated lr-chart-3d documentation measures 21,603,769 unpacked UI bytes in CI; its ceiling retains the 612-byte shared-artifact allowance at the next 64-byte boundary (21,604,416). The regenerated editor data measures 1,693,693 packed bytes in CI; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary (1,693,696). The same editor data measures 10,501,855 unpacked bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary (10,501,888). The current map companion archive measures 4,006,821 unpacked bytes in CI; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary (4,006,848). Separating the map feature loaders measures 21,604,865 unpacked UI bytes; its ceiling retains the 612-byte shared-artifact allowance at the next 64-byte boundary (21,605,504). Its regenerated editor data measures 1,693,817 packed bytes, so the packed ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary (1,693,824). The same editor data measures 10,502,837 unpacked bytes, so the unpacked ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary (10,502,848). The model viewer and shared renderer contracts measure 21,661,155 unpacked UI bytes; its ceiling advances to 21,661,824 bytes, the next 64-byte boundary after the 612-byte companion-pack allowance. The 13 model-viewer strings measure 6,174,756 unpacked translation bytes; its ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary at 6,174,784 bytes. Model-viewer editor metadata measures 1,696,826 packed bytes and 10,521,742 unpacked bytes; the two IDE ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundaries at 1,696,832 and 10,521,792 bytes. The map image catalog, GeoJSON overlays, and lifecycle corrections measure 21,680,520 unpacked UI archive bytes and 21,681,132 estimated bytes; the UI ceiling advances to 21,681,152, the next 64-byte boundary after the 612-byte shared-artifact allowance. Deferred map initialization, theme overlays, basemap selectors, pointer events and drawing measurements measure 21,722,087 unpacked UI archive bytes and 21,722,699 estimated bytes; the UI ceiling advances to 21,722,752 bytes, the next 64-byte boundary after the existing 612-byte shared-artifact allowance. Five map messages measure 6,187,611 unpacked translation bytes; its ceiling advances to 6,187,648 bytes. Updated map editor metadata measures 1,699,515 packed and 10,530,552 unpacked bytes; the IDE ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundaries at 1,699,520 and 10,530,560 bytes. Explicit highlighter engines and live map updates measure 21,743,643 unpacked UI archive bytes and 21,744,255 estimated bytes; the UI ceiling advances to the next 64-byte boundary at 21,744,256 bytes. Updated editor metadata measures 1,700,049 packed and 10,535,021 unpacked bytes; only those IDE ceilings advance to the next 64-byte boundaries at 1,700,096 and 10,535,040 bytes. Map composition, lazy feature boundaries and source replacement measure 21,799,151 unpacked UI archive bytes and 21,799,763 estimated bytes; only the unpacked ceiling advances to 21,799,808, the next 64-byte boundary. Matching translations measure 6,187,763 unpacked bytes and editor metadata measures 1,700,103 packed and 10,535,164 unpacked bytes; their failing ceilings advance to 6,187,776, 1,700,160 and 10,535,168 bytes. Other ceilings remain unchanged.
